assumptions: These are proposed, not executed, tests. No implementation, pytest outcome, deployed environment or real notification delivery is evidenced.
Only the sign-in card is image-observed. Treat name@example.com and ******** as presentation examples, not proven prefilled credentials; recovery views, navigation and synthetic sign-in are proposed.

The approved design selects an injected aware UTC clock, locked process-local store, private link outbox separate from the owner-notification sink, normalized-key private accounting, and a rolling 3600-second window; these are not prescribed by the wireframe or the recovery standard.
Choose distinct P_old, P_new1, P_new2 and P_new3 that meet the implementation's documented minimal password rule; choose P_invalid that it rejects. Do not assume a password-complexity threshold.
Use independent fresh stores and clients for comparisons unless a case explicitly calls for continued state; the private outbox is a test-only inspection surface, not external delivery.
A review of a bounded tree/diff and available execution records cannot prove no deployment outside those records. Unavailable runtime, tests or records are validation problems, not passes.
Approved REQ and TASK identifiers come from prior stages, whose authorized reads supplied no citable stage_output locator; none is invented.

open_questions.question: What exact minimal password-validation rule will the implementation document?
open_questions.context: Select valid and invalid test data only after the rule is documented; empty input is invalid for the proposed reset form.

open_questions.question: What wording and precise focus/error treatment should the proposed recovery views use?
open_questions.context: Only the sign-in image is observed; tests assert account-neutral, accessible outcomes rather than unsupported copy or pixels.

open_questions.question: Will issued links be inspectable only in tests or through a local-only demonstrator affordance?
open_questions.context: The approved design uses a private owner-directed outbox, never public confirmation or external mail.

open_questions.question: Is the design-selected rolling 3600-second window and private nonexistent-key accounting acceptable?
open_questions.context: The standard specifies five per account per hour and identical public existing/nonexistent responses, not the internal algorithm.

open_questions.question: What additional sign-in policy or responsive fidelity, if any, is required?
open_questions.context: Synthetic sign-in and a guarded page are proposed solely to observe session revocation; the image establishes neither behavior nor dimensions.

test_cases.title: Observed sign-in card and examples
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh unauthenticated client; no entered credentials. GET the proposed / sign-in page.
Inspect the visible card, rendered HTML, label/input associations, field types, displayed examples and initial input values.
expected_results: One centered outlined sign-in card on a white page has a bold Sign in heading, programmatically labeled Email address and Password fields, a visible name@example.com example and a masked ******** example.
Examples are presentation hints, not populated credentials: initial inputs are empty and no plaintext password example is exposed. No exact dimensions or sign-in behavior are inferred.

test_cases.title: Observed sign-in control order
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh unauthenticated client; GET the proposed / page.
Inspect visual and DOM order of Password, recovery link, submit button and administrator sentence; check their relative visual treatment without pixel measurements.
expected_results: A blue underlined Forgot password? link follows Password; a dark full-width Sign in button follows the link; gray No account? Contact your administrator. appears beneath the button.
Wording and order match the image; button presence does not establish an authentication policy.

test_cases.title: Start reset request from recovery link
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh unsigned-in client on the sign-in page; focus its Forgot password? link with Tab.
Activate the link with Enter and inspect the proposed /forgot-password destination, address field, submit action and focus order.
expected_results: The link opens a server-rendered reset-request form with a programmatically labeled editable address field and operable submit control rather than a dead end.
Focus order reaches the address and submit controls. Only the originating link is image-observed; its destination is proposed.

test_cases.title: Existing and nonexistent request response parity
steps: Preconditions/data: separate matched fresh stores and clients at fixed UTC t0 = 2026-01-01T12:00:00Z, with zero request history; synthetic A owner@example.test and absent N absent@example.test. Match headers, valid per-client CSRF and pre-POST cookie state; use syntactically valid differently normalized addresses.

Submit A and N independently at the same fixed time. Record public status, Location, response body, account-dependent headers/cookies, and followed redirect destination; repeat with execution order and client assignment swapped on new matched fixtures.
Inspect each private outbox separately from public responses.
expected_results: For every matched pair, public status, Location, destination status/body and account-dependent headers/cookies are identical; no address or bearer token is echoed. Compare equivalent CSRF cookie attributes rather than unrelated random bytes.
Only A obtains a private owner-directed link. Clock advancement, previous cookie state, throttling history and run order cannot explain any public difference.

test_cases.title: Suppress the sixth request within an hour
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh synthetic A owner@example.test, empty private outbox/counter, injected aware UTC t0 = 2026-01-01T12:00:00Z and a CSRF-valid client.
Submit five eligible requests for A's normalized key at t0, refreshing CSRF if required; record public responses and private link count.
At t0 + 3599 seconds submit a sixth and inspect outbox, honored-issuance count and public response.
expected_results: The first five requests produce five distinct private A links; the sixth adds no link and is not honored.
The sixth has the same neutral valid-request public status, redirect, destination and account-dependent headers/cookies as the first five; throttle state is not exposed.

test_cases.title: First, fifth and rolling-hour boundary requests
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh A store, empty history, injected UTC t0 = 2026-01-01T12:00:00Z, valid CSRF per request. Submit one A request and four more at t0.
Inspect private outbox after first and fifth; attempt sixth at t0 + 3599 seconds and another exactly t0 + 3600 seconds.
Compare public responses for first, fifth, suppressed sixth and boundary request.
expected_results: One then five distinct private links exist after first and fifth; the sixth adds none. At the proposed rolling boundary, timestamps <= t - 3600 seconds age out and the next eligible request adds a link.
All syntactically valid public responses remain the same neutral response. Exact oldest-timestamp arithmetic is a design choice, not a standard-mandated window algorithm.

test_cases.title: Valid link changes only owner password
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh synthetic A owner@example.test and B peer@example.test with separate P_old fixture hashes at UTC t0; privately issue an unused A link. Select distinct P_new1 satisfying the documented minimal password rule.
Before t0 + 30 minutes, GET the private link using a new client, obtain valid form CSRF and POST P_new1.
Inspect A/B hashes and attempt synthetic sign-in for A with P_old and P_new1 and B with its original credential.
expected_results: Success is reported only after commit: A's hash changes, A's old credential fails and P_new1 succeeds in the proposed demonstration.
B's hash and credential remain unchanged. Private link inspection and synthetic sign-in do not imply external delivery or a production authentication policy.

test_cases.title: Consumed link cannot change password again
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh A link at t0, clock before expiry; choose distinct documented-valid P_new1 and P_new2, valid CSRF and empty owner-notice sink.
Redeem the link with P_new1, recording hash, session version and notice count; GET and CSRF-valid POST the same link again with P_new2.
Inspect non-success view, hash, version, notices and the effective credential.
expected_results: Second GET offers no usable password form but a new-request path; second POST cannot report success.
Replay does not change hash or session version and adds no notice; P_new1 remains effective. Concurrent replay is separately checked in TC-022.

test_cases.title: Link valid at last instant before expiry
steps: Preconditions/data: isolated unused A link issued at aware UTC t0 = 2026-01-01T12:00:00Z, documented-valid P_new1 and valid form CSRF obtained before expiry.
At t0 + 30 minutes - 1 microsecond POST P_new1 and inspect result, A hash and proposed synthetic old/new sign-in behavior.
expected_results: The proposed strict now < issue + 30 minutes check accepts the unused link; exactly one password change commits.
A changed hash and old-password rejection/new-password acceptance corroborate the success; success text alone is insufficient.

test_cases.title: Exact expiry and valid GET followed by expired POST
steps: Preconditions/data: three separate fresh unused A links issued at UTC t0, documented-valid P_new1, valid per-client CSRF; snapshot hash, token state, session version and notices.
In store 1 GET and POST at t0 + 30 minutes; in store 2 POST at t0 + 30 minutes + 1 microsecond; in store 3 GET the valid form at t0 + 29 minutes and POST with its CSRF at exactly t0 + 30 minutes.
Inspect each response and private state.
expected_results: No case commits a password change, successfully consumes the token, bumps the session version, records a notice or claims success.
Expiry-time GET offers a recoverable new-request path; a prior valid GET does not authorize an expired POST, which rechecks time at commit.

test_cases.title: Revoke all owner sessions but not another account
steps: Preconditions/data: via proposed synthetic sign-in, independently authenticate A on clients A1 and A2 and B on B1; confirm initial guarded access, save A1's signed cookie and snapshot versions.
Using a separate client, issue and successfully redeem A's unused link before expiry with valid CSRF and documented-valid P_new1.

Request the guarded page with A1, A2, B1 and a fresh jar containing A1's stale cookie; separately inspect A's version and check failed, expired and replayed resets against an otherwise valid A session.
expected_results: A's version increments once and both previous A clients plus the copied signed cookie are unauthenticated on their next guarded request; B1 stays authorized and B's version is unchanged.
Failed, expired or replayed resets do not revoke a valid A session; a valid cookie signature does not bypass the account-version guard.

test_cases.title: Exactly one owner notice for a successful reset
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh A/B fixtures and empty distinct in-memory owner-notification sink; obtain one unused A link from the private outbox, valid form CSRF and documented-valid P_new1.
Reset A before expiry; inspect committed hash and process-local notice sink independently of the public response.
expected_results: Exactly one owner-addressed A notice corresponds to the committed A reset; none is for B and there are no extra entries.
Public success follows commit. A local sink entry is not real, durable or externally delivered notification.

test_cases.title: One separate notice for each of two successes
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh A and empty sink; choose distinct documented-valid P_new1 and P_new2, separate valid CSRF and clock before expiry of each link.
Issue A link L1 and reset with P_new1; issue fresh L2 after success and reset with P_new2; inspect the sink after each commit.
Replay consumed L1 and inspect sink again.
expected_results: After first success there is one A-owner record; after second there are two distinct records for the two committed resets.
Replaying L1 produces no third notice or success. Only the local sink, not external delivery, is verified.

test_cases.title: Python 3.12 Flask server-rendered pages
steps: Preconditions/data: once implementation artifacts exist, inspect runtime/dependency metadata and proposed Flask app factory/Jinja templates; prepare local Python 3.12 without deploying.
Under Python 3.12 use a Flask test client to request sign-in, reset-request and usable/unusable proposed link pages; inspect content types, response HTML and template-rendering path.
expected_results: Runtime metadata targets Python 3.12, Flask is the framework and requested user-facing pages return server-rendered HTML containing the relevant forms/states, not client-only rendering.
Unavailable Python 3.12 or missing artifacts is a validation problem, not a pass or a reason to deploy.

test_cases.title: Synthetic accounts and process-local notification sink
steps: Preconditions/data: inspect fixture sources and integrations; create two independent proposed app instances with synthetic A/B fixtures and empty private outboxes and distinct notice sinks at fixed UTC t0.
In instance 1 privately issue and redeem an A link; compare both instances' accounts, counters, token records, outboxes, versions and sinks.
Inspect integrations for real identity lookup, external notification service or persistent account/notification backend.
expected_results: Only synthetic fixtures are used; the owner notice exists in instance 1's separate in-memory sink, not instance 2's. Links, counters, token, version and password mutations do not cross instances.
No external notification service is invoked; a private test link outbox is distinct from the notice sink and proves neither durability nor delivery.

test_cases.title: Collect and run automated pytest coverage
steps: Preconditions/data: only after implementation and tests exist, under Python 3.12 collect pytest cases, inspect assertions and map each required behavior to test names.
Run pytest locally; record command, environment, collection and actual pass/fail/skip/blocked outcome for each targeted behavior group.
expected_results: Automated assertions cover sign-in presentation, reset entry, existing/nonexistent and throttled parity, first/fifth/sixth/hour boundary, successful reset, single-use/replay, just-before and exact 30-minute expiry, all-session sign-out and an owner notice after each success.
Collection alone is not a pass; missing, skipped or failing assertions remain reported gaps. This proposed case does not assert pytest has run or passed.

test_cases.title: Document synthetic prototype production limitations
steps: Preconditions/data: once project documentation exists, inspect README, local run/test instructions and all production-readiness claims.

Check for synthetic-only identities, volatile process-local accounts/counters/tokens/session versions/link outbox/notice sink, restart/multi-worker divergence, lack of real delivery and incomplete production security.
expected_results: Documentation explicitly identifies synthetic and in-memory limitations, gives local/test instructions, and does not claim production readiness or durable/external delivery.
Absent documentation or an unqualified production-ready claim fails this future review; the checklist is not a production security certification.

test_cases.title: Bounded no-deployment review
steps: Preconditions/data: obtain final bounded project tree/diff and available execution/delivery records; do not deploy, trigger workflows or contact a hosted environment.

Inspect added workflows, deployment scripts/configuration, hosted endpoints and deploy commands; distinguish local Flask execution or pytest from deployment. Record reviewed paths/records and inaccessible environments.
expected_results: No deployment workflow or performed deployment is found within the inspected deliverables and available records; flag any deployment-related addition.
Inspection cannot prove absence of deployments outside those records; missing external evidence is a stated limit, never a global non-deployment claim.

test_cases.title: Parity under limit and throttling with normalized keys
steps: Preconditions/data: for each comparison use separate matched stores and independent clients with equivalent valid CSRF/headers/cookie state; fix UTC t0 and seed normalized existing A owner@example.test and absent N absent@example.test keys with equal private counts of zero, four or five at t0. Use mixed-case/whitespace variants normalized to baseline keys.

At counts zero and four submit one valid request per key at t0; at five submit one per key at t0 + 3599 seconds. Follow redirects; repeat each pair with order and client assignment swapped on fresh matched stores.
Compare public status, Location, confirmation body and account-dependent headers/cookies; inspect private counts/outboxes separately.
expected_results: For every matched A/N pair, account-dependent public surfaces are indistinguishable below and at the ceiling; they disclose neither account existence nor issuance. CSRF randomness, wall time and run order cannot explain differences.
Eligible A alone gets a private link; N never does; neither suppressed key gets a link. Proposed private normalized-key accounting cannot be bypassed by case/whitespace variants.

test_cases.title: Invalid address, password and CSRF rejection
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh matched A/N stores and CSRF-capable clients; snapshot counters, outbox, A hash, token state, version and notice sink. Choose empty/malformed address, empty password and P_invalid rejected by the eventual documented rule.
Submit empty/malformed address for A/N-equivalent paths, comparing feedback within each input class; submit an otherwise valid request with missing or invalid CSRF on fresh clients.
Obtain an unused A link privately; POST empty/P_invalid passwords with valid CSRF and a documented-valid password with missing/invalid CSRF; inspect responses and captured state.
expected_results: Invalid addresses have readable field-associated, account-independent feedback; untrusted CSRF requests are rejected without issuing a link. No particular invalid-input HTTP status or equality between different invalid-value classes is prescribed.
Invalid passwords have field-associated feedback; rejected request/reset inputs do not change hash, consume token, bump session version, record notice or claim success.

test_cases.title: Concurrent fifth/sixth issuance ceiling
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh A with four honored links at fixed UTC t0, two independent CSRF-valid clients and synchronized test barrier; hold clock at t0 + 1 second.
Release two concurrent valid requests for normalized A (one mixed-case variant); inspect both public responses and locked private count/outbox.
expected_results: Exactly one additional link is issued, totaling five; no interleaving permits six or duplicate issuance.
Both public responses are indistinguishable on account-dependent surfaces and reveal neither winner nor throttle state.

test_cases.title: Concurrent redemption commits at most once
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh unused A link at t0, clock held at t0 + 1 minute; two clients with independent valid CSRF and distinct documented-valid P_new1/P_new2; snapshot A hash/version and empty notice sink.
Release simultaneous POSTs to the same token using a barrier; compare responses, final hash, consumed token, session version and notices.
expected_results: Exactly one POST commits and may claim success; the loser cannot report success or overwrite the winner's password, whose chosen credential alone authenticates.
The token is consumed once, A's version changes once and exactly one A-owner notice is appended; fixed time excludes expiry as the cause.

test_cases.title: Notification failure rolls back process-local reset
steps: Preconditions/data: fresh unused A link, two independently active A sessions and one B session, valid CSRF and documented-valid P_new1 before expiry; snapshot hash, token, versions and sink. Inject an in-process sink-append failure, including a variant throwing after partial append.
Submit the otherwise valid reset and inspect public result, private state and guarded access from A's two clients and B's client.
expected_results: No success is claimed and no inconsistent partial success remains: A hash, token usability, A/B versions and sink contents match the pre-call snapshot, including no orphan notice after partial append.
A and B sessions retain pre-failure access. This is a proposed process-local rollback check, not a durable distributed-transaction claim.

test_cases.title: Keyboard, labels, errors and announced outcomes
steps: Preconditions/data: keyboard-only client and accessibility-tree/screen-reader inspection for pictured sign-in and proposed request, confirmation, new-password, success and unusable-link views; arrange empty/invalid inputs and expired link.
Tab and keyboard-activate links, submit and retry controls in each view; inspect focus order, visible focus, accessible names/labels and readable contrast.
Trigger invalid input and success/non-success transitions; inspect field-error association and whether focus reaches or announces each outcome.
expected_results: No keyboard trap; implemented views have logical focus order, visible focus, programmatic labels, discernible button/link names and readable contrast.

Errors are readable and associated with fields; outcomes are focused or announced; success is never announced before commit and unusable links never announce success. These behaviors and recovery views are proposals, not image-observed facts.

test_cases.title: Unusable tokens and issued-link non-disclosure
steps: Preconditions/data: separate fixtures with unknown opaque token, consumed A token and unused A token at t0 + 30 minutes; prepare valid CSRF and documented-valid P_new1 for attempted POSTs and snapshot hashes, versions and sink.

GET and POST each token; inspect response, cookies, HTML, ordinary logs, headers and outgoing asset URLs. Independently issue an eligible A link and inspect public request/confirmation and private outbox.
Inspect proposed token-page Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, absence of third-party assets and redaction of token path segments in ordinary logs.
expected_results: Unknown, used and expired token URLs yield recoverable non-success/new-request behavior without password mutation, version bump, notice or success claim. Issued tokens occur only in the private process-local test outbox, not public confirmation, cookies, ordinary logs or page body.
Token-page policies and log/asset constraints match approved design proposals; a private outbox proves neither external link delivery nor production-grade confidentiality.
